title: Final vertices characterized by right anodyne inclusions
statement: Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Call a simplicial map right anodyne if it belongs to the smallest class containing the horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, and all isomorphisms, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Let $J$ be a quasicategory and $t\in J_0$ a vertex. Then the inclusion $\{t\}\cong\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ is right anodyne if and only if $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is weakly contractible for every vertex $j\in J_0$.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 4.7.3.22 (02J5), equivalence (1) and (3); final object has the mapping-space meaning of Definition 4.7.3.1 in Subsection 4.7.3. Right anodyne convention: Variant 4.2.4.2, also spelled out in the proof of Proposition 4.3.6.4 (018J). Read online, not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; Stacks does not provide this quasicategorical statement. Mapping-space convention check: Kerodon Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX), Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0), and Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5). The natural pinch-inclusion equivalences identify the right-pinched model used here with the unadorned Hom spaces used in the cited cofinality/finality statements; after taking opposites use the left-pinch comparison as well.

proof.text: Assume $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is weakly contractible for every $j$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone] to obtain $F:J^{\triangleright}\to J$ restricting to $\operatorname{id}_J$ and constant at $t$ on $\{t\}^{\triangleright}$. Denote the base inclusions by $b:J\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleright}$ and $a:\{t\}\hookrightarrow\{t\}^{\triangleright}$, and the constant map by $q:\{t\}^{\triangleright}\to\{t\}$. Then $Fb=\operatorname{id}_J$ and $qa=\operatorname{id}_{\{t\}}$.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, (1) to (2), using the normalized slice-section criterion.

proof.text: Write $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow J$ and $e=i^{\triangleright}:\{t\}^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleright}$. The map $i$ is degreewise injective, so [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] makes $e$ right anodyne. The pairs $(a,b)$ and $(q,F)$ define maps of arrows $i\to e\to i$: the first square commutes by functoriality of the cone, and the second because $Fe=iq$, the normalization of $F$. Their composite on the domain is $qa=\operatorname{id}$ and on the codomain is $Fb=\operatorname{id}$. Thus $i$ is a retract of $e$, and is right anodyne by the retract clause in its definition. This proves the mapping-space condition implies right anodyneness.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, (2) to (3): the displayed retract diagram, using the right-cone lemma.

proof.text: Conversely assume $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow J$ is right anodyne. Apply the pushout-join assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] with $A=\{t\}$, $B=J$, $K=\varnothing$, and $L=\Delta^0$. Since $X\star\varnothing=X$, it states that the inclusion $m:M=J\amalg_{\{t\}}\{t\}^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleright}$ is inner anodyne. Define $h:M\to J$ to be $\operatorname{id}_J$ on the first summand and the constant map at $t$ on the second. The two maps agree on $\{t\}$, so the pushout supplies $h$.

The quasicategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] extends maps from each inner horn into $J$. This extension property holds for the whole weakly saturated class defining inner anodyne maps in [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]: for an isomorphism use its inverse; for a pushout extend on the attached summand and glue; for a transfinite composite choose compatible extensions successively and use the colimit at limit stages; for a retract compose the map with the retraction of domains, extend across the larger arrow, and restrict along the section of codomains. Consequently $h$ extends across $m$ to $F:J^{\triangleright}\to J$. Because $F$ extends $h$, it is the identity on $J$ and constant at $t$ on $\{t\}^{\triangleright}$, including its cone point and degenerate identity edge. The reverse implication of [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone] now makes every $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ weakly contractible. Together with step 2 this proves the equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, (3) to (2), extension into an inner-horn-filling target; then the normalized cone criterion.
